subject: Response window amendment request — FastPay migration week (P1/P2 on-call split)
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fastpay.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fastpay.com
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary response-window amendment during migration week

Mateo / Redwood team,

Quick context: FastPay will be performing a cross-region database migration the week of Aug 2. Our SRE leads expect elevated alert noise and a higher likelihood of false P1s while traffic rebalances. We want to avoid cascading PagerDuty escalations overnight while the migration completes (estimated 48–72 hours).

Can Redwood support a temporary adjustment to our P1/P2 response windows for that maintenance window? Specifically we are asking for: 
- P1: 30-minute initial touch instead of the usual 15 minutes during 00:00–06:00 PDT on Aug 3–5
- P2: extend from 2 hours to 4 hours for the same overnight window

We understand credits may apply; procurement is looped. Our goals: reduce noisy pages, keep critical on-call focused on real incidents, and preserve the normal SLOs outside the migration window.

Attaching a short migration plan and runbook for your review.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Site Reliability | FastPay Inc.
[Attachment: fastpay-migration-plan.pdf (PDF)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fastpay.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary response-window amendment during migration week

Liam — thanks for the heads-up and the plan. I reviewed the migration timeline; the request is reasonable provided we put a short, documented carveout in place and an explicit escalation runway for anything that looks user-impacting.

Proposed approach (quick bullets):
- Approve temporary response-window amendment for Aug 3 00:00–Aug 5 06:00 PDT with the exact windows you requested (P1 initial touch -> 30m; P2 -> 4h).
- Require a pre-migration readiness call 24 hours before the window where we agree on noisy-alert suppression rules and list of endpoints that must always page.
- Maintain the normal on-call chain for the daytime hours; for overnight coverage we propose an on-call split: Redwood covers primary triage for infra alerts between 00:00–03:00, FastPay on-call owns 03:00–06:00 (this is configurable). Proposed schedule attached (proposed-oncall-split.csv).
- Include a rollback criterion: if any production payment processing pipeline shows >0.1% error spike sustained for 10 minutes, we immediately revert to standard SLOs and escalate to P0 ops bridge.
- We'll prepare an SLA amendment draft and a short runbook; please review.

If you want us to formalize this, I'll ask Marissa for sign-off on the contract amendment + any credit terms. Sergio, can you weigh in on overnight coverage and whether we need to staff an extra Redwood on-call for those nights?

Mateo
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-oncall-split.csv (CSV)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: temporary response-window amendment during migration week

Marissa / Sergio — forwarding FastPay's request and my proposed approach. Key points for approval:
- Temporary amendment Aug 3 00:00 -> Aug 5 06:00 PDT (P1 touch 30m / P2 4h overnight)
- Pre-migration readiness call + agreed noisy-alert suppression list
- On-call split: Redwood 00:00–03:00, FastPay 03:00–06:00 (we can flip if needed)
- Rollback trigger (0.1% sustained error for 10m => revert)
- We will draft a short SLA amendment and run DocuSign for signatures; procurement is looped.

Operational asks from Redwood:
- Approve the temporary carveout and sign the amendment (legal/contracting will need to sign later; I can draft).
- Confirm whether we should schedule an additional Redwood on-call for Aug 3 overnight to reduce fatigue risk. I estimate 1 additional engineer per night would cost ~6 hours of overtime per night vs offering a small credit.

Sergio — any objections to the coverage split? If you approve, I will schedule the readiness call (24h prior) and attach the SLA amendment draft to an email to procurement.

—Mateo

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@fastpay.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fastpay.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary response-window amendment during migration week — APPROVED (draft amendment attached)

Liam / team —

We approve the temporary response-window amendment as proposed. Thanks for providing the migration plan and the rollback rules — sensible guardrails. A few operational commitments from Redwood:
- Amendment effective: Aug 3 00:00 PDT -> Aug 5 06:00 PDT; P1 initial touch 30m nights, P2 window 4h nights. Normal SLOs resume outside the window.
- Redwood will participate in the 24-hour readiness call and maintain primary triage for 00:00–02:59 PDT. FastPay will cover 03:00–06:00 PDT (per the proposed split). If during scheduling we determine FastPay needs earlier handover, we'll update the amendment.
- We will prepare a one-page SLA amendment and send via DocuSign by EOD tomorrow for signature. Procurement, please review the credit language (we propose a one-time operational credit in lieu of longer-term SLA changes).
- Attachment: draft amendment + short runbook. Please confirm you have the same rollback trigger (0.1% sustained error for 10 minutes).

Sergio — I approved an extra Redwood on-call for the first night only (Aug 3) to reduce the ramp risk. Please coordinate scheduling with Mateo and mark the extra coverage in Ops.

Liam — once you confirm, we'll send the DocuSign link and calendar invites for the readiness call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: sla-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX)]
